bull_bear.body:
- Flagship "Aamcol" brand recognised for precision-engineered gear-cutting tools
- Broad product portfolio spanning gear hobs for multiple gear types plus inspection tools and precision accessories, reducing dependence on a single product segment
- Diverse customer base across automobile, gearbox, machine tool and other engineering industries
- Products stated to meet international standards, supporting import substitution and supply to international markets
- Productivity initiatives — retrofitting, reconditioning, automation, improved utilisation of high-speed cutting tools and cycle time optimisation
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intense competition from domestic and international manufacturers — Management flags competition as leading to pricing pressures and margin constraints in a business whose products compete against imported precision tooling.
- Raw material price and availability volatility — Volatility in the prices and availability of key raw materials, particularly high-speed steel (HSS), carbide, alloy steel and other specialty metals, may impact production costs and profitability; the Company's stated mitigation is strengthening procurement, holding strategic inventory and diversifying the supplier base.
- Foreign exchange exposure on imported inputs and exports — Fluctuations in foreign exchange rates affect the cost of imported raw materials and the competitiveness of exports. The Company had foreign exchange outgo of Rs. 1120.27 Lakhs in FY2025-26 and plans to import 4 machines from overseas for the next expansion phase, so the exposure is two-sided.
- Dependence on cyclical end-user industries — Demand is derived from automobiles, industrial machinery, capital goods, aerospace and defence; any slowdown in those end-user industries directly reduces demand for the Company's gear hobs and cutting tools. Management describes itself as prone to market vagaries and unique economic cycles.
- Technology obsolescence requiring continuous reinvestment — Rapid technological advancement requires continuous investment in modern machinery, product development, automation and R&D to remain competitive - a structural capital demand on a company that is already funding expansion partly through promoter and bank loans.
- Product and customer concentration — The Company's own mitigation strategy is framed as product diversification and customer diversification to 'reduce dependence on any single product segment or customer' and to reduce concentration risk, indicating that the revenue base is concentrated in a narrow product set and customer group.
- Global economic uncertainty, geopolitical tension and supply chain disruption — Trade restrictions and supply chain disruptions may adversely affect customer demand and export markets, which management identifies as a growth avenue.
- Shortage of skilled manpower and rising labour costs — A skilled-labour shortage and increasing labour costs may affect productivity and operational efficiency in a precision-engineering operation dependent on skilled machining.
- Regulatory and policy change — Changes in government policies, taxation, environmental regulations, import-export policies and compliance requirements may influence business operations and costs - particularly relevant given the reliance on imported inputs and export markets.
- Execution and ramp risk on the expansion programme — The Expansion Project is only substantially complete: commercial production has commenced for certain products while the remaining product lines are still to ramp in a phased manner, and a further Next Phase of Expansion of approximately Rs 10 crore is being funded by internal accruals plus promoter and bank loans.

business.body: Jainex Aamcol manufactures precision-engineered gear-cutting tooling — gear hobs for spur and helical gears, chain sprockets, timing pulleys and worm gears — along with cutters, inspection tools and precision accessories, all sold under the "Aamcol" brand. Its customers span automobile manufacturers, industrial and special gearbox manufacturers, machine tool manufacturers and other engineering sectors. The Company positions its products as meeting international standards, contributing to import substitution while also supplying international markets.

outlook.body:
- Enhance manufacturing capability through technology upgradation, process automation, product innovation and continuous quality improvement
- Complete and ramp the Expansion Project - increase installed capacity of the existing portfolio, add Shaper Cutters, Master Gears and Skiving Cutters, and improve quality of Big Module Hobs and Worm Wheel Hobs
- Undertake a Next Phase of Expansion to add more products to the Gear Cutting Tools Basket that have good export potential
- Expand the product portfolio and develop value-added precision tooling solutions to reduce dependence on any single product segment or customer (product diversification)
- Strengthen the domestic and international customer base and increase presence in global / export markets
- Invest in advanced manufacturing technologies, research and development, workforce skill enhancement and digitalization to improve productivity, operational efficiency and customer satisfaction
- Run productivity enhancement initiatives - retrofitting, reconditioning, automation, improved utilisation of high-speed cutting tools and cycle time optimisation
- Position as an import-substitution supplier of world-class quality tooling in place of imported precision tooling
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Jainex Aamcol has substantially completed its Expansion Project. During FY2025-26 the civil construction for the project was completed and all the machinery required for the expansion was installed; trial production was successfully carried out and commercial production of certain products has commenced, with the remaining product lines expected to begin commercial production in a phased manner based on production schedules and market requirements. The stated objectives of the project are to increase the installed capacity of the existing product portfolio, enable production of new products including Shaper Cutters, Master Gears and Skiving Cutters, improve the quality of Big Module Hobs and Worm Wheel Hobs, and enhance overall production efficiency. The Board believes successful implementation will significantly enhance production capacity, improve product quality and broaden the product portfolio. Separately, the Directors have embarked on a Next Phase of Expansion which will add more products with good export potential to the Gear Cutting Tools Basket: 4 machines are to be acquired from overseas and 2 CNC machines locally, at a cost of approximately Rs 10 crore, funded by internal accruals, loans from promoters and loans from banks. The Directors' Report states in one place that this Next Phase will be completed within the current financial year and in another that it is expected to be complete in 2027; management says it would enable the Company to increase its turnover substantially. The Company also implemented productivity enhancement initiatives including retrofitting, reconditioning, automation, improved utilisation of high-speed cutting tools and cycle time optimisation.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global gear manufacturing market valued at approximately USD 88.8 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 139.8 billion by 2034, a CAGR of around 5.0%, driven by industrial automation, expanding automotive production, renewable energy investment and demand for high-precision mechanical components
- Industrial gearbox market - a key end-user segment for gear-cutting tools - estimated at USD 31.9 billion in 2025 and expected to reach USD 45.5 billion by 2033 at a 4.8% CAGR, with Asia-Pacific accounting for over 40% of global demand
- Indian gear market valued at approximately USD 1.8-2.0 billion in 2025 and expected to grow at a 7-9% CAGR over the next five years, supported by passenger vehicle, commercial vehicle and EV production, industrial equipment and rising engineering-goods exports
- Indian auto-components industry reported turnover of Rs. 3.56 lakh crore in the first half of FY 2025-26 (April-September 2025), 6.8% year-on-year growth, with exports up 9.3% to USD 12.1 billion
- Automotive sector growth - rising production of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, EVs and two-wheelers - is the primary demand driver for gears and gear-cutting tools
- Industrial automation, CNC machining, robotics and Industry 4.0 adoption accelerating demand for high-precision cutting tools, inspection tools and precision accessories
- Government initiatives - Make in India, PLI schemes, PM Gati Shakti and increased infrastructure spending - encouraging domestic manufacturing and capacity expansion
- Expansion of capital goods and engineering industries (industrial machinery, railways, defence, aerospace, renewable energy, heavy engineering) creating sustained demand for precision tooling solutions
- Import substitution and localisation: Indian manufacturers increasingly replacing imported tooling solutions with domestically manufactured products
- Export opportunity from global supply chain diversification and the China+1 strategy; Indian engineering exports resilient in key markets including the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia
- Technological advancement in gear manufacturing processes, high-speed machining, advanced tool coatings and precision inspection technologies driving demand for technologically advanced gear hobs and cutting tools
- Management states the industry outlook remains positive and that the Company is well positioned to leverage emerging opportunities in both domestic and international markets
- Policy backdrop: India initiated formulation of the Automotive Mission Plan 2047 (AMP 2047) in mid 2025 via seven expert-led sub-committees targeting milestones for 2030, 2037 and 2047, aligned to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jainex Aamcol Limited is a manufacturer of gear hobs, special cutting tools, inspection tools and precision accessories under its flagship "Aamcol" brand, serving engineering and manufacturing industries in India and export markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Jainex Aamcol manufactures precision-engineered gear-cutting tooling — gear hobs for spur and helical gears, chain sprockets, timing pulleys and worm gears — along with cutters, inspection tools and precision accessories, all sold under the "Aamcol" brand. Its customers span automobile manufacturers, industrial and special gearbox manufacturers, machine tool manufacturers and other engineering sectors. The Company positions its products as meeting international standards, contributing to import substitution while also supplying international markets.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global gear manufacturing market valued at approximately USD 88.8 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 139.8 billion by 2034, a CAGR of around 5.0%, driven by industrial automation, expanding automotive production, renewable energy investment and demand for high-precision mechanical components
- Industrial gearbox market - a key end-user segment for gear-cutting tools - estimated at USD 31.9 billion in 2025 and expected to reach USD 45.5 billion by 2033 at a 4.8% CAGR, with Asia-Pacific accounting for over 40% of global demand
- Indian gear market valued at approximately USD 1.8-2.0 billion in 2025 and expected to grow at a 7-9% CAGR over the next five years, supported by passenger vehicle, commercial vehicle and EV production, industrial equipment and rising engineering-goods exports
- Indian auto-components industry reported turnover of Rs. 3.56 lakh crore in the first half of FY 2025-26 (April-September 2025), 6.8% year-on-year growth, with exports up 9.3% to USD 12.1 billion
- Automotive sector growth - rising production of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, EVs and two-wheelers - is the primary demand driver for gears and gear-cutting tools
- Industrial automation, CNC machining, robotics and Industry 4.0 adoption accelerating demand for high-precision cutting tools, inspection tools and precision accessories
- Government initiatives - Make in India, PLI schemes, PM Gati Shakti and increased infrastructure spending - encouraging domestic manufacturing and capacity expansion
- Expansion of capital goods and engineering industries (industrial machinery, railways, defence, aerospace, renewable energy, heavy engineering) creating sustained demand for precision tooling solutions
- Import substitution and localisation: Indian manufacturers increasingly replacing imported tooling solutions with domestically manufactured products
- Export opportunity from global supply chain diversification and the China+1 strategy; Indian engineering exports resilient in key markets including the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia
- Technological advancement in gear manufacturing processes, high-speed machining, advanced tool coatings and precision inspection technologies driving demand for technologically advanced gear hobs and cutting tools
- Management states the industry outlook remains positive and that the Company is well positioned to leverage emerging opportunities in both domestic and international markets
- Policy backdrop: India initiated formulation of the Automotive Mission Plan 2047 (AMP 2047) in mid 2025 via seven expert-led sub-committees targeting milestones for 2030, 2037 and 2047, aligned to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Enhance manufacturing capability through technology upgradation, process automation, product innovation and continuous quality improvement
- Complete and ramp the Expansion Project - increase installed capacity of the existing portfolio, add Shaper Cutters, Master Gears and Skiving Cutters, and improve quality of Big Module Hobs and Worm Wheel Hobs
- Undertake a Next Phase of Expansion to add more products to the Gear Cutting Tools Basket that have good export potential
- Expand the product portfolio and develop value-added precision tooling solutions to reduce dependence on any single product segment or customer (product diversification)
- Strengthen the domestic and international customer base and increase presence in global / export markets
- Invest in advanced manufacturing technologies, research and development, workforce skill enhancement and digitalization to improve productivity, operational efficiency and customer satisfaction
- Run productivity enhancement initiatives - retrofitting, reconditioning, automation, improved utilisation of high-speed cutting tools and cycle time optimisation
- Position as an import-substitution supplier of world-class quality tooling in place of imported precision tooling

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Jainex Aamcol has substantially completed its Expansion Project. During FY2025-26 the civil construction for the project was completed and all the machinery required for the expansion was installed; trial production was successfully carried out and commercial production of certain products has commenced, with the remaining product lines expected to begin commercial production in a phased manner based on production schedules and market requirements. The stated objectives of the project are to increase the installed capacity of the existing product portfolio, enable production of new products including Shaper Cutters, Master Gears and Skiving Cutters, improve the quality of Big Module Hobs and Worm Wheel Hobs, and enhance overall production efficiency. The Board believes successful implementation will significantly enhance production capacity, improve product quality and broaden the product portfolio. Separately, the Directors have embarked on a Next Phase of Expansion which will add more products with good export potential to the Gear Cutting Tools Basket: 4 machines are to be acquired from overseas and 2 CNC machines locally, at a cost of approximately Rs 10 crore, funded by internal accruals, loans from promoters and loans from banks. The Directors' Report states in one place that this Next Phase will be completed within the current financial year and in another that it is expected to be complete in 2027; management says it would enable the Company to increase its turnover substantially. The Company also implemented productivity enhancement initiatives including retrofitting, reconditioning, automation, improved utilisation of high-speed cutting tools and cycle time optimisation.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Flagship "Aamcol" brand recognised for precision-engineered gear-cutting tools
- Broad product portfolio spanning gear hobs for multiple gear types plus inspection tools and precision accessories, reducing dependence on a single product segment
- Diverse customer base across automobile, gearbox, machine tool and other engineering industries
- Products stated to meet international standards, supporting import substitution and supply to international markets
- Productivity initiatives — retrofitting, reconditioning, automation, improved utilisation of high-speed cutting tools and cycle time optimisation

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Intense competition from domestic and international manufacturers — Management flags competition as leading to pricing pressures and margin constraints in a business whose products compete against imported precision tooling.
- Raw material price and availability volatility — Volatility in the prices and availability of key raw materials, particularly high-speed steel (HSS), carbide, alloy steel and other specialty metals, may impact production costs and profitability; the Company's stated mitigation is strengthening procurement, holding strategic inventory and diversifying the supplier base.
- Foreign exchange exposure on imported inputs and exports — Fluctuations in foreign exchange rates affect the cost of imported raw materials and the competitiveness of exports. The Company had foreign exchange outgo of Rs. 1120.27 Lakhs in FY2025-26 and plans to import 4 machines from overseas for the next expansion phase, so the exposure is two-sided.
- Dependence on cyclical end-user industries — Demand is derived from automobiles, industrial machinery, capital goods, aerospace and defence; any slowdown in those end-user industries directly reduces demand for the Company's gear hobs and cutting tools. Management describes itself as prone to market vagaries and unique economic cycles.
- Technology obsolescence requiring continuous reinvestment — Rapid technological advancement requires continuous investment in modern machinery, product development, automation and R&D to remain competitive - a structural capital demand on a company that is already funding expansion partly through promoter and bank loans.
- Product and customer concentration — The Company's own mitigation strategy is framed as product diversification and customer diversification to 'reduce dependence on any single product segment or customer' and to reduce concentration risk, indicating that the revenue base is concentrated in a narrow product set and customer group.
- Global economic uncertainty, geopolitical tension and supply chain disruption — Trade restrictions and supply chain disruptions may adversely affect customer demand and export markets, which management identifies as a growth avenue.
- Shortage of skilled manpower and rising labour costs — A skilled-labour shortage and increasing labour costs may affect productivity and operational efficiency in a precision-engineering operation dependent on skilled machining.
- Regulatory and policy change — Changes in government policies, taxation, environmental regulations, import-export policies and compliance requirements may influence business operations and costs - particularly relevant given the reliance on imported inputs and export markets.
- Execution and ramp risk on the expansion programme — The Expansion Project is only substantially complete: commercial production has commenced for certain products while the remaining product lines are still to ramp in a phased manner, and a further Next Phase of Expansion of approximately Rs 10 crore is being funded by internal accruals plus promoter and bank loans.
